summary: The trend filter is intact (SPY 5.6% above its 200-day), but leadership is narrowing to defensives and tech is being sold, so keep normal exposure without adding appetite. Favor defensive and broad-breadth exposure over Nasdaq and growth, and size new risk modestly.
reasons: Regime is on: SPY closed 763.96 vs a 200-day of 723.62, 5.58% above, so the long-only trend test passes. SPY is only -0.5% over 21 days and +3.64% over 63 days, so this is a pause, not a breakdown.

Growth is the weak spot: QQQ is -3.23% over 5 days and -4.96% over 21 days, against SPY at -1.01% and -0.5%. XLK is -6.66% (21d) and XLC -4.57% (21d), both still falling over 5 days (-3.62% and -4.46%). News memory from 10-20 to 10-22 shows the AI/data-center complex under pressure, consistent with this.

Breadth is better than the index suggests: equal-weight RSP is +1.5% (5d) and +3.27% (21d), 6.02% above its 200-day, while cap-weighted SPY is negative. The weakness is concentrated in mega-cap tech, not the broad market.

Rotation is defensive: XLP leads at +9.17% (21d, +3.82% 5d), followed by XLE +8.34%, XLU +7.85% and XLV +7.41%. Staples, utilities and health care leading while tech and communication lag is a risk-averse pattern, not a risk-on one.

Small caps are not confirming strength: IWM is -1.86% (21d), -4.73% (63d) and sits at -0.14% vs its 200-day, right on the line. Industrials are also weak (XLI -1.98% 21d, -8.48% 63d, 3.27% below its 200-day).

Volatility is edging up from a low base: VIXY is +7.93% (5d) and +5.42% (21d). It is still -17.44% over 63 days and 26% below its 200-day, so there is no stress signal yet. SPY 20-day realized vol is 9.85% vs 12.73% over 252 days, so the market is calm in absolute terms.

Rates are the cross-current: TLT is +2.21% (5d) and +2.0% (21d), so long yields have eased this week, but TLT is still 1.9% below its 200-day and -0.64% over 63 days. HYG is -0.84% (21d), 1.02% below its 200-day, and LQD is 1.55% below its 200-day: credit is soft but not breaking. News memory cites a 10-year near 5.14%, hike odds and Brent above $110, so inflation and rate risk remain.

Gold is not acting as a haven: GLD is -3.58% (5d), -6.08% (21d), 10.96% below its 200-day, with 28.7% annual volatility. The dollar is firm (UUP +0.87% 21d, 3.68% above its 200-day), which usually pressures gold and international stocks.
Internationals are lagging: VXUS is -3.71% (21d) and VWO is -5.44% (21d), both near or below their 200-days (-0.22% and -2.28%).

asset_class_view.equity_etfs: Prefer broad US exposure (VOO +5.61% above its 200-day, VTI +5.12%) over QQQ (-4.96% 21d, 20% annual vol). Equal-weight breadth is healthier than cap-weight, which favors a broad core over a growth tilt. Avoid adding VXUS and VWO (-3.71% and -5.44% over 21d, at or below their 200-days) and IWM (on its 200-day, -4.73% over 63d). VNQ is bouncing (+1.31% 21d) but is -7.29% over 63d and sits on its 200-day (-0.44%), so it is not yet attractive.
asset_class_view.bonds_gold: Bonds are the one sleeve rallying: TLT +2.0%, IEF +1.47%, BND +1.13% over 21 days, with low volatility for BND (4.0%) and IEF (5.0%). They are still below their 200-days (BND -0.67%, IEF -1.49%, TLT -1.9%), so a modest allocation to BND or IEF makes sense. Add TLT cautiously, since it carries 9.6% volatility and the rate-hike backdrop. Gold is risky: GLD is -6.08% (21d) and 10.96% below its 200-day, so do not buy the dip yet.
asset_class_view.crypto: Cautious. BTC is +11.36% over 63 days and 11.7% above its 200-day but -4.17% over 21 days, with 44% annual volatility. ETH is -11.8% over 21 days, only 10.75% above its 200-day, and carries 61% volatility. News memory shows BTC rejected near $84.3k and recovering from a roughly 6% correction. Keep crypto positions small; BTC is preferable to ETH.

watch: SPY closing below its 200-day of 723.62 (about 5.6% lower) would turn the stance risk-off and trigger the code filter.
QQQ losing its 200-day (currently 4.26% above) or XLK's slide extending past -10% over 21 days would signal the tech weakness is spreading to the index.
VIXY rising well beyond +8% in 5 days alongside a falling RSP would signal real risk-off; RSP turning negative on 5 days would end the breadth support.
HYG breaking further below its 200-day (currently -1.02%) while TLT falls would mean credit and rate stress together.
A recovery in QQQ and XLK with staples giving back gains would move the stance toward risk-on.
Oil and rate-hike headlines (Brent above $110, 10-year near 5.14%) per news memory: a sharp rise would hit the duration sleeve and growth.
